question.text: According to interest rate parity, a currency with a HIGH interest rate will trade at a ______ in the forward/futures market.

answer.text: It depends on the central bank policy

explanation.text: The Logic: The future value of a currency with a high interest rate is at a discount to a currency with a low interest rate. For example, INR (higher interest rate) is at a forward discount to USD (lower interest rate), and similarly EUR can be at a discount to JPY. The Trap: A common misconception is that high interest rates make a currency strong in forwards. In fact, the high-yielding currency trades at a forward discount. Note: Because INR has higher interest rates than USD, USDINR forward and futures prices trade above the spot rate.
